name: Long-term ultra-low-temperature frozen storage of tuna meat at -45 °C or lower to prevent metmyoglobin (browning) formation
plain_name: Store sashimi tuna deep-frozen cold enough that its red colour does not turn brown
description: Nakazawa et al. (Int. J. Refrigeration 2020) stored low-pH and high-pH tuna meat at a range of frozen-storage temperatures over long periods: metMb% rose in low-pH meat held warmer than -40 °C, while no increase occurred at -45 °C or lower regardless of pH, supporting ultra-low-temperature storage of tuna.
keywords: Store sashimi tuna deep-frozen cold enough that its red colour does not turn brown

sources.citation: Nakazawa N, Wada R, Fukushima H, Tanaka R, Kono S, Okazaki E (2020). Effect of long-term storage, ultra-low temperature, and freshness on the quality characteristics of frozen tuna meat. Int J Refrigeration 112:270-280. doi:10.1016/j.ijrefrig.2019.12.012

requirements.rationale: Colour stability (no metMb increase) needs storage at -45 °C (228.15 K) or colder; either a documented range reaching that low or a documented lowest temperature settles it.
Storage warmer than -40 °C (233.15 K) increased metMb in low-pH meat; optional because the -45 °C requirement already covers it.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
